title: From Route to Response: How Drugs Move and Work
next: Chapter 7, Lesson 3: Medication classes and the BC drug list

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you gave drugs by mouth, under the tongue, inhaled, into the muscle and into the nose. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Compare routes and their speed, and what the IV changes
  2. Follow a drug through the body: pharmacokinetics
  3. See how drugs act, and why you reassess after every dose

Textbook: Chapter 7, PDF pages 466–495
slides.say: Welcome back. As an EMR you've already used several routes: ASA by mouth, nitroglycerin under the tongue, salbutamol by inhaler or nebulizer, epinephrine into the muscle, and naloxone into the nose. Now that you're practising as a PCP, you add the fastest and riskiest route, the IV, and you need to understand why drugs behave the way they do. Today we'll compare the routes, follow a drug through the body, which is called pharmacokinetics, and look at how drugs act, which is called pharmacodynamics. This is the science behind a rule you'll hear all the time: reassess after every dose.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。当 EMR 时你已经用过好几种给药途径：口服 ASA、舌下硝酸甘油、用吸入器或雾化器给沙丁胺醇、肌注肾上腺素、鼻内给纳洛酮。现在以 PCP 身份执业，你多了最快也最有风险的途径——静脉（IV），你需要理解药物为什么会有这样的表现。今天我们比较各种给药途径，跟踪药物在体内的过程，这叫药代动力学；再看药物怎样起作用，这叫药效动力学。这就是你会反复听到的那条规矩背后的科学：每给一剂都要复评。

slides.title: The drug profile: know it first
slides.body:
• Names and class; mechanism of action
  • Indications and contraindications
  • Dose, route, and form: solution, suspension (shake it), tablet, patch
  • Onset, duration, side effects
  • Special groups: children, older adults, pregnancy

Store drugs out of the sun at about 15–30 °C. Controlled drugs: locked, unmarked cabinet, every use recorded.
slides.say: Every drug comes with a medication profile, and as a PCP you should know it for each of your drugs. It gives the names and the class, and the class explains many side effects. It gives the mechanism, which is how the drug works, the indications, which are the reasons to give it, and the contraindications, when giving it will most likely cause harm. It lists the dose, the route, and the form. Most paramedic drugs are solutions, fully dissolved. A suspension settles, so shake it first. Store drugs out of the sun at about fifteen to thirty degrees, and keep controlled drugs locked, with every use recorded.
slides.sayZh: 每种药都附有药物档案（medication profile），作为 PCP，你对自己的每一种药都应该熟悉它。档案写明药名和分类，分类能解释很多副作用；写明作用机制，也就是药怎样起效；写明适应症，即给药的理由；还有禁忌症，即给了很可能造成伤害的情况。它还列出剂量、途径和剂型。paramedic 用的药大多是溶液，药物完全溶解；混悬液会沉淀，用前要摇匀。药物要避光、在大约十五到三十度保存；受控药物要上锁，每次使用都要登记。

slides.title: Routes and how fast they work
slides.body:
RouteFamilyOnset
IVparenteral30–60 s
Inhaled, SL spraypercutaneous3 min
SL tabletpercutaneous3–5 min
IMparenteral10–20 min
SCparenteral15–30 min
Oral (PO)enteral30–90 min
On the skinpercutaneoushours to days

Times assume normal perfusion.
slides.say: Routes fall into three families. Percutaneous means through the skin or a mucous membrane, like under the tongue, in the nose, or into the lungs. Enteral means through the gut, mostly by mouth. Parenteral means everything else, usually with a needle: IV, IM, and subcutaneous. Now the speed, in a person with normal perfusion. An IV drug works in thirty to sixty seconds. Inhaled drugs and a sublingual spray take about three minutes, a nitroglycerin tablet three to five. IM takes ten to twenty minutes, subcutaneous fifteen to thirty, and a pill by mouth thirty to ninety. That's why the mouth is rarely used in emergencies, with one big exception: chewed ASA for chest pain.
slides.sayZh: 给药途径分三大类。经皮/黏膜途径（percutaneous）指经过皮肤或黏膜，比如舌下、鼻内、吸入肺部。肠道途径（enteral）指经过消化道，主要是口服。肠外途径（parenteral）指其余所有途径，通常用针：静脉、肌注和皮下。再看速度，前提是灌注正常：静脉给药三十到六十秒起效；吸入药和舌下喷雾约三分钟，硝酸甘油舌下片三到五分钟；肌注十到二十分钟，皮下十五到三十分钟，口服三十到九十分钟。所以急救时很少口服给药，只有一个大例外：胸痛时嚼服 ASA。

slides.title: IV: fastest and most dangerous
slides.body:
IV = fastest, most precise, most dangerous

  • The whole dose hits the blood at once: toxicity is more likely
  • Push slowly unless the protocol says otherwise
  • Never inject by direct needle stick: risk of infiltration
  • Slower to reach targets in heart failure or deep shock
  • BC example: naloxone acts in 1 min IV vs 3 min IM or IN
slides.say: The IV is your new route as a PCP, and it is both the best and the most dangerous. It's the fastest, and it gives you the most control over the dose. But the whole dose enters the blood at once, so if it's the wrong drug or the wrong dose, a toxic reaction is much more likely. That's why most IV drugs are pushed slowly unless your protocol says otherwise. Never inject a drug with a needle straight into a vein; use an established IV line, or the drug may leak into the tissue, which is called infiltration. A BC example of the speed: naloxone works in about one minute IV, but about three minutes IM or intranasal.
slides.sayZh: 静脉是你作为 PCP 的新途径，它既是最好的，也是最危险的。它最快，对剂量的控制也最精确。但整剂药一下子全部进入血液，如果药错了或剂量错了，发生毒性反应的可能大得多。所以大多数静脉药要缓慢推注，除非流程另有规定。绝不要拿针直接扎进静脉推药，要通过已建立的静脉通路，否则药物可能漏进组织，这叫外渗（infiltration）。BC 的一个速度例子：纳洛酮静脉给约一分钟起效，肌注或鼻内约三分钟。

slides.q: You're a PCP. A known diabetic is unresponsive with a blood glucose of 2.6 mmol/L. Your partner manages the airway. What is your best treatment?
options: Apply glucose gel to the cheek and gums
Start an IV and give D10W
Give glucagon first, even though an IV is possible
Give 15 g of oral glucose by mouth
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. A known diabetic is unresponsive. The blood glucose is two point six, and your partner is managing the airway. You're a PCP. What is your best treatment? A, apply glucose gel to the cheek and gums. B, start an IV and give D10W. C, give glucagon first, even though an IV is possible. D, give fifteen grams of oral glucose by mouth. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一位已知糖尿病人没有反应，血糖二点六，搭档在管理气道。你是 PCP，最好的处理是什么？A 把葡萄糖凝胶涂在颊部和牙龈；B 建立静脉通路，给 D10W；C 先给胰高血糖素，尽管能开静脉；D 口服十五克葡萄糖。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. In the BC diabetic protocol, the PCP obtains vascular access and corrects confirmed low blood sugar with D10W, ten to twenty-five grams, which acts almost immediately. A and D are wrong because oral glucose and gel are only for patients alert enough to protect their own airway; this patient could choke. C is wrong because for a PCP, glucagon is the backup when an IV can't be obtained, and it takes about fifteen minutes to work.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。按 BC 糖尿病急症流程，PCP 建立静脉通路，用 D10W 纠正已证实的低血糖，剂量十到二十五克，几乎立即起效。A 和 D 错，因为口服葡萄糖和凝胶只适用于神志足以自己保护气道的病人，这位病人可能会呛到。C 错，因为对 PCP 来说，胰高血糖素是开不了静脉时的后备，而且大约要十五分钟才起效。

slides.title: Pharmacokinetics: the drug's journey
slides.body:
Absorption→Distribution→Biotransformation→Excretion

What the body does to the drug

  • Faster absorption with good blood flow and a thin, large surface
  • Higher concentration: faster absorption
  • Deep shock: absorption is delayed by any route
  • Bioavailability: how much active drug reaches the target
slides.say: Pharmacokinetics is what the body does to the drug, in four steps: absorption, distribution, biotransformation, and excretion. Absorption is how the drug gets from where you put it into the blood. It's faster where blood flow is good and the surface is large and thin, like the single cell layer lining the intestine, and slower through thick layers like the skin. Here's the clinical point: in deep shock, blood is pulled away from the skin and muscles, so absorption can be delayed by any route. Bioavailability means how much of the drug is still active when it reaches its target.
slides.sayZh: 药代动力学是身体对药物做了什么，分四步：吸收、分布、生物转化和排泄。吸收是药物从给药部位进入血液的过程。血流好、表面积大而薄的地方吸收快，比如只有单层细胞的肠道内壁；穿过皮肤这类多层组织就慢。临床要点是：深度休克时，血液从皮肤和肌肉撤走，任何途径的吸收都可能延迟。生物利用度是指药物到达靶点时仍有活性的量。

slides.title: Distribution: only free drug works
slides.body:
Only free drug can act

  • Drug bound to albumin (a blood protein) is parked, inactive
  • Low albumin (e.g. liver disease): more free drug, stronger effect
  • Fat, muscle, and bone can store drug
  • Blood–brain barrier: lets in lipid-soluble drugs only
  • The placenta blocks many drugs, but not all
slides.say: Distribution is how the drug spreads through the body, carried by the blood. If cardiac output is low, or the patient is cold and blood is shunted away from the skin, the drug moves slowly. Here is a key idea: only free drug works. Many drugs ride on albumin, a large protein in the blood, and while they're bound they are parked and inactive. If a patient has less albumin, for example from liver disease, more drug is free, and the same dose can act stronger. And there are barriers. The blood–brain barrier lets only fat-soluble drugs into the brain. The placenta blocks many drugs, but not all, so pregnancy always needs thought.
slides.sayZh: 分布是药物随血液在全身扩散的过程。心输出量低，或者病人很冷、血液从皮肤撤走时，药物移动就慢。一个关键概念：只有游离的药物才起作用。很多药会搭在白蛋白——血液里的一种大分子蛋白——上，结合着的时候就像「停车」，没有活性。如果病人白蛋白少了，比如因为肝病，游离药就多，同样剂量的作用会更强。体内还有屏障：血脑屏障只让脂溶性药物进入大脑；胎盘能挡住很多药，但不是全部，所以孕妇用药总要多想一步。

slides.title: Liver and kidneys: clearing the drug
slides.body:
• Liver turns drugs into metabolites or water-soluble forms
  • First-pass effect: swallowed drugs pass the liver first
  • That's why insulin can't be taken by mouth
  • Kidneys excrete most drugs in the urine
  • Kidney failure: drug builds up to toxic levels

Loading dose: a big first dose to reach the target level fast. Maintenance dose: keeps it there.
slides.say: Next, the body clears the drug. Biotransformation happens mostly in the liver, which turns the drug into a metabolite or a more water-soluble form that's easier to remove. Blood from the gut goes to the liver before anywhere else. This is the first-pass effect: the liver can weaken or destroy a swallowed drug before it reaches the body. That's why insulin is never given by mouth, and why some oral doses are bigger. Then the kidneys excrete most drugs in the urine. If the kidneys fail, a normal dose can build up to toxic levels. The book also describes a loading dose to reach the target level fast, and a maintenance dose to keep it there.
slides.sayZh: 接下来，身体要清除药物。生物转化主要在肝脏进行，肝把药物变成代谢物或更易溶于水、更容易排出的形式。来自胃肠的血液先流经肝脏，再去别处。这就是首过效应：口服的药在到达全身之前，可能已被肝脏削弱甚至完全灭活。所以胰岛素从不口服，有些口服剂量也更大。然后由肾脏把大多数药物随尿排出。肾衰竭时，正常剂量也可能蓄积到中毒水平。书里还讲到用负荷剂量迅速达到目标浓度，再用维持剂量保持住。

slides.title: Pharmacodynamics: what the drug does
slides.body:
Agonistfits the receptor, turns it onsalbutamol on beta-2
Antagonistsits in the receptor, blocks itnaloxone on opioid receptors
Affinityhow tightly it bindsthe stronger one wins
  • Therapeutic index = LD50 ÷ ED50; close to 1 = dangerous
  • Half-life: time for the body to remove half the drug
slides.say: Pharmacodynamics is the other direction: what the drug does to the body. An agonist fits the receptor and turns it on, like salbutamol opening the airways through beta-2 receptors. An antagonist sits in the receptor and blocks it, like naloxone keeping opioids off their receptors. Affinity is how tightly a drug binds; when two chemicals compete, the stronger one wins. Two safety numbers matter. The therapeutic index compares the dose that kills half of a test population with the dose that works in half. The closer it is to one, the smaller the safety margin. The half-life is the time the body needs to remove half of the drug.
slides.sayZh: 药效动力学是反方向：药物对身体做了什么。激动剂配上受体并把它打开，比如沙丁胺醇通过 β2 受体打开气道。拮抗剂占住受体并把它堵上，比如纳洛酮不让阿片类药物接触受体。亲和力是药物结合得有多牢；两种化学物质竞争时，亲和力强的赢。两个安全数字很重要：治疗指数是让一半受试对象死亡的剂量和对一半有效的剂量之比，越接近一，安全范围越小。半衰期是身体清除一半药物所需的时间。

slides.title: Expected and unexpected responses
slides.body:
TermMeaning
Side effectunwanted but expected; every drug has some, even oxygen
Allergic reactionmost common unpredictable response; can become anaphylaxis
Idiosyncrasya response unique to one person
Tolerancesame dose, weaker effect; tachyphylaxis = after a few doses
Potentiationone drug boosts another (alcohol + acetaminophen: liver injury)

Summation: 1 + 1 = 2. Synergism: 1 + 1 > 2.
slides.say: Every drug brings more than the effect you want. A side effect is unwanted but expected. Every drug has some, even oxygen, so you weigh the benefit against the risk. An allergic reaction is the most common unpredictable response, and it can become anaphylaxis, so watch for it after any drug. An idiosyncrasy is a strange reaction seen in one person only. Tolerance means the same dose works less over time; tachyphylaxis is tolerance that appears after just a few doses. Drugs also interact. Summation is one plus one equals two. Synergism is one plus one equals more than two. Potentiation is when one drug boosts another, like alcohol with acetaminophen, which can damage the liver.
slides.sayZh: 每种药带来的都不只是你想要的效果。副作用是不想要但可以预见的，每种药都有，连氧气也有，所以要权衡获益和风险。过敏反应是最常见的不可预测反应，可能发展成过敏性休克，所以给任何药之后都要留意。特异质反应是只在个别人身上出现的奇怪反应。耐受是指同样剂量随时间效果变弱；快速耐受是只给了几剂就出现的耐受。药物之间还会相互作用：相加作用是一加一等于二；协同作用是一加一大于二；增效作用是一种药增强另一种药，比如酒精加对乙酰氨基酚会伤肝。

slides.q: Ten minutes after salbutamol, your asthmatic patient breathes easier, but her heart rate rose from 96 to 118 and her hands shake slightly. What is this?
slides.say: Let's try one. Ten minutes after salbutamol, your asthmatic patient is breathing easier, but her heart rate went from ninety-six to one hundred eighteen, and her hands shake a little. What is this? A, an allergic reaction. B, an expected side effect. C, an idiosyncrasy. D, tachyphylaxis. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来做一题。给了沙丁胺醇十分钟后，你的哮喘病人呼吸轻松了，但心率从九十六升到一百一十八，手也有点抖。这是什么？A 过敏反应；B 可预见的副作用；C 特异质反应；D 快速耐受。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B, an expected side effect. Salbutamol targets beta-2 receptors, but some beta-1 effect on the heart is expected, so a faster pulse and a mild tremor are predictable. Note it, keep reassessing, and weigh benefit against risk. An allergic reaction would bring hives, swelling, or worse breathing. An idiosyncrasy is a rare response unique to one person. Tachyphylaxis means the drug stops working after a few doses, but her breathing improved.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B，可预见的副作用。沙丁胺醇针对 β2 受体，但对心脏有一些 β1 作用是预料之中的，所以心率加快、轻微手抖可以预见。记录下来，继续复评，权衡获益与风险。过敏反应会出现荨麻疹、肿胀或呼吸更差。特异质反应是个别人独有的罕见反应。快速耐受是给了几剂后药不管用了，而她的呼吸是改善的。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: routes
slides.body:
From the BC exam drug list and protocols

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • PO: chewed ASA, oral glucose, acetaminophen, ibuprofen
  • Oral mucosa: glucose gel, if the patient can protect the airway
  • SL: nitroglycerin
  • Inhaled: salbutamol, Entonox, methoxyflurane
  • IM: epinephrine, glucagon, naloxone
  • IN: naloxone 4 mg, glucagon 3 mg

PCP adds

  • Vascular access (IV) and fluid boluses
  • IV D10W; IV TXA over 1 minute
  • IV naloxone if still unconscious and apneic
  • Dimenhydrinate IM or IV; diphenhydramine IV or PO
  • Ipratropium in the nebulizer with salbutamol
  • Dexamethasone (PO preferred); ondansetron PO
slides.say: Here's how your routes change. On the left is what every licence level does. By mouth: chewed ASA, oral glucose, acetaminophen, and ibuprofen. Glucose gel on the oral mucosa, but only if the patient can protect the airway. Nitroglycerin under the tongue. Salbutamol, Entonox, and methoxyflurane are inhaled. Epinephrine, glucagon, and naloxone go into the muscle, and naloxone and glucagon can also go into the nose. On the right is what the PCP adds: vascular access and fluid boluses, IV D10W, and IV TXA over one minute. IV naloxone when the patient stays unconscious and apneic. Dimenhydrinate IM or IV, diphenhydramine IV or by mouth, ipratropium with salbutamol, dexamethasone, and ondansetron.
slides.sayZh: 看看你的给药途径怎么变化。左栏是所有执照级别都做的。口服：嚼服 ASA、口服葡萄糖、对乙酰氨基酚和布洛芬。口腔黏膜涂葡萄糖凝胶，但只限能自己保护气道的病人。舌下含硝酸甘油。吸入沙丁胺醇、笑气（Entonox）和甲氧氟烷。肌注肾上腺素、胰高血糖素和纳洛酮，其中纳洛酮和胰高血糖素也可以鼻内给。右栏是 PCP 增加的：静脉通路和快速补液，静脉给 D10W，静脉推 TXA、一分钟推完；病人持续昏迷且无呼吸时静脉给纳洛酮；茶苯海明肌注或静脉，苯海拉明静脉或口服，异丙托溴铵与沙丁胺醇合用，还有地塞米松和昂丹司琼。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• IV drugs can't be taken back: six rights before you push
  • Infiltration: check the site; leaked D10W can kill tissue
  • Dimenhydrinate IV: dilute, push slowly over about 2 min
  • TXA: 2 g over 1 min; faster can drop the BP
  • Shock or hypothermia: drugs may absorb late or not work yet
  • Reassess patient and IV every 5–15 minutes
slides.say: Here's what's new to watch out for. First, an IV drug can't be taken back, so run the six rights before you push, not after. Second, infiltration. The BC monograph warns that D10W leaking into the tissue can cause tissue death. Third, some IV drugs have a speed limit. Dimenhydrinate is diluted and pushed slowly over about two minutes. TXA, two grams, goes over one minute, because pushing it faster can drop the blood pressure. Fourth, in shock or hypothermia, drugs may absorb late, or not work until the patient warms up. And BC's IV maintenance procedure has you reassess the patient and the IV every five to fifteen minutes.
slides.sayZh: 新的注意事项如下。第一，静脉药推进去就收不回来，所以要在推药之前、而不是之后核对六个正确。第二，外渗：BC 药物专论提醒，D10W 漏进组织会造成组织坏死。第三，有些静脉药有速度限制：茶苯海明要稀释后在大约两分钟内缓推；TXA 两克要一分钟推完，推太快会让血压下降。第四，休克或低体温时，药物可能吸收延迟，或者要等病人复温后才起效。BC 的静脉维护流程还要求每五到十五分钟复评一次病人和静脉通路。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• BC exam: IV access; no IO procedure and no tracheal drugs
  • Book: SC epinephrine for mild asthma. BC: epinephrine IM only
  • Anaphylaxis with low BP: BC still gives epinephrine IM
  • Methoxyflurane: 3 mL, may repeat after 20 min, max 6 mL; not under 18
  • Low blood sugar: BGL below 4.0 mmol/L; IV sugar is D10W only
slides.say: For the BC exam, here is where the book and BC differ. The book teaches the intraosseous route and drugs given down a tracheal tube. The BC licensing exam has no procedure for starting an IO, and no tracheal drugs, so IV access is your route; IO is BCEHS added scope. The book says epinephrine can be given under the skin for mild asthma; in BC, epinephrine is intramuscular only. The book also warns against IM injections when perfusion is poor, but the BC anaphylaxis protocol still gives IM epinephrine to a hypotensive patient, and the PCP adds IV fluids. Methoxyflurane in BC is three millilitres, repeated after twenty minutes if needed, to a maximum of six, and never under eighteen. And for low blood sugar, BC treats a level below four point zero, with D10W as the only IV sugar.
slides.sayZh: 备考 BC，看看书和 BC 哪里不一样。书里讲骨髓腔（IO）途径，以及经气管导管给药，BC 执照考试没有开 IO 的操作规程，也没有经气管给药，所以考试时用静脉（IV）通路；BCEHS 的 PCP 经扩展范围（Schedule 1）培训后可以做 IO。书里说轻度哮喘可皮下注射肾上腺素；BC 的肾上腺素只用肌注。书里还提醒灌注差时不要肌注，但 BC 过敏性休克流程对低血压病人仍然肌注肾上腺素，PCP 再加静脉补液。BC 的甲氧氟烷是三毫升，必要时二十分钟后可重复，最多六毫升，十八岁以下禁用。低血糖方面，BC 以血糖低于四点零为准，静脉补糖只有 D10W。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. IV is fastest and most dangerous: six rights before you push
  2. Absorb, distribute, transform, excrete; only free drug works
  3. Expect side effects, watch for allergy, reassess every dose

Next: medication classes and the BC drug list
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: the IV is your fastest and most precise route, and also the most dangerous, so check the six rights before you push. Two: pharmacokinetics is what the body does to the drug: absorption, distribution, biotransformation, and excretion. Only free drug works, and shock, a weak liver, or failing kidneys change the picture. Three: pharmacodynamics is what the drug does to the body. Expect side effects, watch for allergic reactions after any drug, and reassess after every dose. Next lesson: medication classes, and reading your patient's own pill bottles. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 记住三件事。一，静脉是最快、最精确的途径，也是最危险的，所以推药前要核对六个正确。二，药代动力学是身体对药物做了什么：吸收、分布、生物转化和排泄；只有游离药物起作用，休克、肝功能差或肾衰竭都会改变局面。三，药效动力学是药物对身体做了什么：预料到副作用，给任何药后都留意过敏反应，每一剂之后都要复评。下节课讲药物分类，以及怎样读懂病人自己的药瓶。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
